purpose: Single-player top-down roguelike game with a real-time ECS combat engine, procedural dungeon generation, an embedded in-game tooling suite (map/entity/spell/spawner editors), and LLM-powered NPC dialogue via OpenAI.

actors.name: Player
actors.description: Single user interacting via keyboard and mouse in a desktop window

external_systems.name: OpenAI Responses API
external_systems.description: LLM-powered NPC dialogue generation using GPT-5 Nano via the Responses API

external_systems.name: WebSocket Server
external_systems.description: Optional multiplayer server (configured, not yet implemented in this repo)

external_systems.name: Local Filesystem
external_systems.description: SQLite database, JSON data files, binary assets (sprites, audio, tiles), log files

containers.name: roguelike_engine
containers.responsibility: Low-level engine layer with no game logic. Provides camera, map (MVC), tiles (MVC), zone (MVC), buildings (MVC), audio service, SQLAlchemy DB engine/models, cache (memory + file), console (MVC), diagnostics overlay, input normalization, z-layer pipeline, world persistence, and engine-level config.

containers.name: roguelike_game
containers.responsibility: Game logic layer. Owns the ECS world (~50 update + ~30 render systems), entity factories (player + monster), staged initialization pipeline, game-loop managers (events, update, render, shutdown), and game-level config.

containers.name: roguelike_editors
containers.responsibility: In-game overlay editors for authoring content at runtime: map, tiles, buildings, entities, FSM, spells, spawner, particles, lighting. Each editor follows MVC with commands and event patterns.

containers.name: roguelike_ui
containers.responsibility: Reusable UI primitives consumed by game and editors: panels, widgets (button, grid, text input, list panel, tab panel, toolbar, hover, icon cache, file picker), HUD components, formatting services, JSON persistence services.

containers.name: minigames
containers.responsibility: Self-contained minigames (Pylos, Soluna) launchable from the main game.

containers.name: SQLite Database
containers.responsibility: Persistent relational storage for game catalog data, migrated from JSON sources.

containers.name: JSON Data Files
containers.responsibility: Content-driven game data not suitable for relational storage: map zone overlays, building instances/templates/collisions, particle instances, light presets/instances, inventory drops, FSM configs, world saves, input bindings.

components.name: ECSWorld
components.description: Central ECS registry. Manages entity IDs (int), component store, spatial index, and ordered update/render system pipelines. Exposes get_entities_with(), create_entity(), remove_entity(), and update()/render() entry points.

components.name: ComponentRegistry
components.description: Dict[ComponentType, Dict[EntityId, Component]] providing O(1) component lookup and efficient entity queries by component intersection (iterates over smallest component set).

components.name: SpatialIndex
components.description: Broadphase spatial hashing over map solid tiles and building collision rects. Rebuilt lazily (invalidate_spatial_index / rebuild_spatial_index) to avoid per-frame cost when map state is static.

components.name: SystemRegistry
components.description: Ordered factory functions (get_update_system_classes, get_render_system_classes) that return the full system pipeline. Render order is overridable via ecs-z-order.json. All systems are benchmarked via pre-built closures.

components.name: GameInitializer
components.description: 22-stage sequential startup pipeline with LoadingScreen visual feedback. Each stage is a pure function injected via a list of (label, fn) tuples, making it testable and extensible without modifying the core.

components.name: GameLoop
components.description: 60 FPS main loop. Calls handle_events → update → update_ecs → render → render_ecs in order, with BenchmarkGroup instrumentation on each phase.

components.name: PlayerFactory
components.description: Builder + Facade for assembling player entities. Reads class stats from DB Entity definition, assembles Position, Health, Mana, CombatStats, Inventory, Sprite, Hitbox, and all other required components.

components.name: MonsterFactory
components.description: Builder + Facade for assembling NPC/hostile entities from DB entity definitions. Supports behavior loading, sprite loading, physics calibration, and per-class FSM assignment.

components.name: InputSystem
components.description: Reads player keyboard/mouse input and translates to component mutations (movement intent, spell cast intent, dash, chat open). Key bindings loaded from data/config/input_bindings.json.

components.name: SpellCastingSystem
components.description: Resolves CastIntent components against the active spell bar, checks mana, applies cooldown, and routes to the appropriate spell-specific system (FireballSystem, LightningSystem, etc.).

components.name: FSMSystem
components.description: Drives NPC Finite State Machines (Idle, Patrol, Aggro, Attack, Flee, Death) each frame. FSM definitions stored as JSON in data/fsm/ and authored via the in-game FSM editor.

components.name: SpawnerRuntimeSystem
components.description: Executes active spawner wave logic: reads SpawnerTemplate + SpawnerWaves from SQLite, generates SpawnRequest components, respects max_count and respawn_seconds constraints.

components.name: AudioSystem
components.description: Consumes audio event queue populated by DamageSfxSystem and other combat systems, delegating to the engine-layer AudioService (Pygame mixer backend).

components.name: Gpt5NanoProvider
components.description: OpenAI Responses API client (Strategy pattern implementation of LLMProvider). Reads OPENAI_API_KEY from env/.env, posts to /v1/responses, parses output_text and tool_calls. 20 s timeout, reasoning effort: low.

components.name: MapService
components.description: MVC controller that builds world maps by combining lobby + dungeon + additional zones, merging them and generating connecting tunnels. Used at startup and during runtime expansion.

components.name: AudioService
components.description: Pygame mixer-backed audio service. Exposes a clean API (play_sfx, play_music, stop) decoupled from ECS. Consumed indirectly via AudioSystem.

main_flows.name: Game Frame Loop
main_flows.description: 60 FPS real-time loop: pygame.event.get → handle_events → update (game state + editors) → ECSWorld.update (all update systems) → render (map, buildings, overlays) → ECSWorld.render (all render systems) → pygame.display.flip()

main_flows.name: NPC Chat (LLM)
main_flows.description: Player presses T → InputSystem enqueues ChatInputEvent → ChatRouterSystem resolves nearest NPC → Gpt5NanoProvider sends POST to OpenAI → LLMResult returned → ChatBubbleRenderSystem displays speech bubble

main_flows.name: Entity Spawn
main_flows.description: SpawnerTriggerSystem fires condition → SpawnerRuntimeSystem reads DB template/waves → SpawnSystem creates entity via MonsterFactory → SpatialIndex invalidated → SpawnStabilizationSystem resolves overlaps

main_flows.name: Spell Casting
main_flows.description: InputSystem queues CastIntent → SpellCastingSystem resolves spell + checks mana → spell-specific system (e.g. FireballSystem) creates projectile entity → HitboxSystem detects collisions → CombatSystem applies damage → DeathSystem handles death → ExperienceSystem grants XP

main_flows.name: Map Overlay Persistence
main_flows.description: MapEditor writes tile changes → save_layers() serializes multi-layer overlay to data/map/zones/overlays/<zone>.overlay.json → on next load, load_layers() reads JSON and rehydrates Map model

main_flows.name: Game Startup (Staged Init)
main_flows.description: launcher.py → init_logging → init_pygame → create_screen → Game.__init__ → GameInitializer (22 stages: display, world, audio, state, map, buildings, ECS, items, editors x8, minimap, renderer, menu) → GameLoop.run()

deployment_nodes.name: Developer Machine
deployment_nodes.logs: logs/  (rotating files: engine, init stage times, profiling)

tech_stack.ecs: Custom hand-rolled ECSWorld (dict-of-dicts, ordered system pipeline)
tech_stack.database: SQLite with WAL journal mode and NORMAL synchronous
tech_stack.migrations: Alembic (10 migration files, content-hash idempotency via import_log)
tech_stack.llm_integration: OpenAI Responses API — gpt-5-nano via urllib (no external SDK)
tech_stack.logging: Python logging with RotatingFileHandler (engine log + stage init log + profiling log)
tech_stack.profiling: Custom BenchmarkGroup decorator — per-frame timings stored in perf_log defaultdict
